tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the loop-factory repo. Edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls, no skills — all tests are fixture-only. Factory code is department-agnostic (no department names in factory/*).

OWNED FILES (only these; all new except the two department registries):
  factory/evalregistry.py
  factory/goldenset.py
  departments/social/runtime/eval_registry.yaml
  departments/podcast/runtime/eval_registry.yaml
  tests/test_evalregistry.py
  tests/test_goldenset.py

CONTEXT — the LOCKED evaluator contract (read wayfinder/drafts/09-evaluator-proposal.md in full): two-tier ladder — deterministic Tier-1 checks first (a Tier-1 fail never reaches a model); Tier-2 model judgment only for content quality, by a DIFFERENT engine than the producer; weighted defects critical/major/minor → verdict block/revise/allow; a Tier-2 evaluator's verdicts may only GATE once it scores clean on a golden set (5-10 fixed cases, open+holdout split) — without a golden set it is advisory-only; registry seeded at factory level with per-department overrides; evaluator drift is an estate concern.

BUILD:
1. factory/evalregistry.py — load + validate an eval_registry.yaml: mapping node_class → {tier1: [check ids], tier2: {required: bool, cross_model: bool, golden_set: path|null, verdict_thresholds: {block_critical: int, block_major: int, revise_major: int}}}. Functions: load_registry(path) -> dict (validated, ValueError naming the bad field); resolve(registry, node_class) -> config with sane defaults (tier2 absent → Tier-1 only); classify_defects(defects, thresholds) -> verdict 'block'|'revise'|'allow' where each defect is {code, severity: critical|major|minor, detail} (unknown severity counts as major — conservative); gating(config, golden_set_passed: bool) -> 'gating'|'advisory' (tier2 required AND golden_set_passed → gating, else advisory when tier2 configured, 'none' otherwise).
2. factory/goldenset.py — golden-set harness, engine-agnostic: load_golden_set(path) -> {open: [cases], holdout: [cases]} from a YAML/JSON file of cases {id, input_summary, expected_verdict, expected_defect_codes?} (validate shapes; at least 5 cases total; both splits non-empty); score(cases, judge_fn) -> {passed: bool, accuracy, failures: [case ids]} where judge_fn(case) returns a verdict string — passed requires 100% on open cases and >= 0.8 on holdout (constants, commented); no model calls in this module — the judge_fn is injected by callers.
3. departments/social/runtime/eval_registry.yaml — real registry for social: node_class draft_qa with tier1 listing social's existing deterministic defect checks by stable ids (read departments/social/runtime/qa_post.py::deterministic_defects and name its check families honestly), tier2 {required: true, cross_model: true, golden_set: null, thresholds: block_critical 1, block_major 3, revise_major 1} — golden_set null means ADVISORY until a golden set lands (that is the locked rule, state it in a comment).
4. departments/podcast/runtime/eval_registry.yaml — podcast: node_classes for its script sensors declaring tier1-only (their executed checks named as ids), tier2 absent — with a comment that script lanes never get model judgment (charter C14).

tests/test_evalregistry.py — at least 8 tests: valid registry loads; bad severity threshold shape names the field; resolve defaults for tier1-only class; classify: one critical → block; majors over threshold → block; majors within revise band → revise; all minor → allow; unknown severity treated as major; gating() advisory without golden set, gating with. tests/test_goldenset.py — at least 5 tests: valid set loads with splits; fewer than 5 cases rejected; score passes on perfect judge; fails when holdout accuracy < 0.8 (fake judge_fn); failure lists the failing case ids. Also: both real department registry YAMLs load cleanly through load_registry (a test must load the actual files).

VERIFY: 'python3 loopfactory.py check' full suite green. You fail for touching files outside the owned list, fewer than 13 total new 'def test_' functions across the two test files, or the verify command failing.
tasks.verified: the locked evaluator contract exists as code: registry + verdict weighting + golden-set gate discipline, with real department registries that load

5. factory/scaffold.py: ensure scaffold copies/instantiates the new templates (eval registry lands at departments/<name>/runtime/eval_registry.yaml); keep existing behavior and CLI flags; department-agnostic.

tests/test_scaffold_inheritance.py — at least 6 tests, run scaffold into tmp_path (read scaffold's existing tests/CLI for the invocation pattern): scaffolded department contains the eval registry file; its charter template carries the setpoints.objectives commented section; its daily script contains the boardfeed and board render steps; the node template mentions runrecord and timed_emit; scaffold remains idempotent-or-refusing on an existing department (match current behavior — read the code and assert what it actually does); scaffolded tree passes 'python3 -m factory.boardfeed' pointed at the tmp repo root without crashing (empty state tolerated).
